suggestions: Replace the raw range-expansion multiplier ((high-low)/Ma((high-low),20)) with a close-location differential: (Ma((close-low)/(high-low),5)-Ma((close-low)/(high-low),20)). Where a stock closes within its daily bar is a smoother, less event-driven proxy for sustained buying/selling pressure than absolute range width, which spikes on earnings, halts, and liquidity shocks and then mean-reverts—those one-day range blowouts are a primary source of day-to-day rank reversals that depress RankIR and year_pos_frac.

Gate the combined signal on multi-horizon momentum agreement before applying the range weight: multiply by (Sign(Diff(close,10)/Std(close,60))*Sign(Diff(close,20)/Std(close,60))) or a soft equivalent Max(0, Sign(...)*Sign(...)). Range expansion during conflicting short- vs medium-term normalized momentum often marks exhaustion or mean-reversion noise rather than persistent pressure; requiring both horizons to align filters whipsaw episodes that flip sign across blocks/years, directly targeting block_pos_frac and RankIR stability without repeating the already-tried daily Sign(Diff(close,1))–range correlation filter.

Bound the momentum leg with a cross-sectionally normalized saturating transform before multiplying: Tanh(Zscore(Diff(close,10)/Std(close,60),60)) * ((high-low)/Ma((high-low),20)). Raw Diff/Std ratios are heavy-tailed and scale-sensitive across volatility regimes, so a few extreme names dominate daily ranks and churn when those outliers revert; compressing the momentum leg limits tail-driven rank jumps and reduces turnover-induced instability, complementing (rather than duplicating) the prior attempt to Rank each leg and smooth the final product.
